principle: Shared safeguards, not 231 separate systems: each failure mode is covered by one of the mechanisms in `safeguards`, and a row leaves OPEN only when a named test in THIS repository proves that mechanism catches it.
honesty: OPEN means not investigated in this repository yet. It does not mean the failure cannot happen, and it does not mean it is uncovered.

The gates A-J are implemented in runner/starters/fullstack-v1/scripts/gates.mjs, not in runner/src, which is why they are easy to miss when reading the runner. Mapping the remaining rows means reading that script against each row; that is the next step and it has not been taken.

Five rows the source inventory recorded as verified cited test files that do not exist here. Two (E03, E04) are genuinely covered by differently-named tests and have been re-cited. Three (F15, F16, F20) depend on a quality ratchet that is absent from this repository and are now recorded as NOT_COVERED_HERE rather than left looking done.

S1.name: Quality scorecard (20 criteria; a verified 10/10 is required before internal approval)
S1.where: runner/src/quality.ts, enforced by the platform at approval
S1.test: runner/test/fullstack.test.ts [AIB-QUALITY] (the scorecard rules themselves); tests/builds-v2.test.ts [AIB-QUALITY] (platform enforcement at approval)

S2.name: Acceptance gates A-J, and website code that cannot forge them
S2.where: the starter's acceptance commands; results in .crestmont/quality/gates.json, trusted only when the runner's own quality-gates check ran this cycle and its bytes match that command's single digest

S3.name: Cross-file contract check (element ids, form fields, endpoint paths)

S4.name: Headless browser check: EVERY .html page under the site root x desktop and mobile (console errors, failed requests, horizontal overflow, nav landmark, screenshots)

S5.name: Persistence check: a success claim must be backed by a durable write

S6.name: Credential scan: no credentials or local secret files in the website's source

S7.name: Brief conformance: the customer's own business details appear on the site

S8.name: Sandbox isolation verified by docker inspect (no network, read-only root, no capabilities, non-root, only the job's mounts)

S9.name: Independent review session (Model A with vision); a verdict is 'unsupported' unless the reviewer actually saw desktop AND mobile screenshots

S10.name: Acceptance evidence record: missing evidence is reported as missing, never as a failing website, and the runner never supplies a status itself

S11.name: Requirement integrity: 'verified' needs evidence, that evidence survives the round-trip through the platform, and the checks that just ran outrank the claim seed

S12.name: Bounded repair loop (cycle limit, repeated failure signature, no measurable progress, ineffective-repair guard), and an overrule that carries its own corrective prompt

S13.name: pending_external: a customer-owned service is never recorded as live; the build waits for the customer instead of faking it

S14.name: Segment continuation: a per-segment limit ends a segment, not the build; 'released' requeues without spending an attempt and resumes from the checkpoint
S14.test: tests/builds.test.ts [AIB-004] (the platform half); runner/test/continuity.test.ts [AIB-CONTINUITY] (the archive half: built and restored from a drive-letter path); runner/test/orchestrator.test.ts [AIB-015] (checkpointed and released without spending an attempt)

quality ratchet.expected: Never lose previously certified functionality; roll back safely when a repair makes the website worse.
quality ratchet.finding: The inventory records F15, F16 and F20 as FIXED_AND_VERIFIED against runner/test/quality-ratchet.test.ts. Neither that test nor any ratchet exists in this tree: `grep -rl ratchet runner/src src` returns nothing. The bounded repair loop (S12) stops a build that stops improving, which is not the same as preserving what was already certified or rolling back a harmful repair.

runner/test/fullstack.test.ts [AIB-QUALI.detail: Three end-to-end tests ('a verified 10/10 ... completes as ready_for_review', 'a score below 10 can never enter internal approval', 'only a provider-side verification missing') fail with "Acceptance checks failed: quality-gates, brief-conformance". Identical on the pristine baseline, so they are not a regression. Every gate test that runs the real gates against a fixture website passes, including all four cross-industry package runs, so what is unproven is the fake-model end-to-end wiring rather than the scorecard rules or the gates.

rows.applicability: applies to the Crestmont AI Website Builder
rows.rootCause: Nothing distinguished an acceptance criterion that FAILED from one with no recorded status, so four consecutive builds were repaired against criteria that were never failing, while the scorecard could not rise above about a third however good the website was.
rows.evidence: Addressed indirectly by the brief contract and brief-conformance check; no per-item verification was done in this assignment.

rows.description: HTML and JavaScript element ID mismatches
rows.applicability: applies to the Crestmont AI Website Builder
rows.rootCause: Generated JS referenced an element id the generated HTML never defined (run 1: getElementById('q-items') vs id='q-message'). Every submit threw a TypeError; nothing reached the server.
rows.prevention: Deterministic cross-file contract check compares every literal getElementById/querySelector('#id') in the site's scripts against the union of ids defined in its pages.
rows.detection: runner acceptance check `contract-check`, run on every build.
rows.recovery: Fails acceptance, so the defect enters the repair loop with a precise message naming the id and the consequence.
rows.evidence: Replays the real defect: run 1's repo FAILS, the brochure starter PASSES. 13/13 tests.

rows.applicability: applies to the Crestmont AI Website Builder
rows.rootCause: Server required a submitted field the form never sent (run 1: worker validated body.items, form posted `message`). Every genuine submission got 422.
rows.prevention: Same contract check compares fields the server treats as REQUIRED against the name= attributes of the site's form controls.
rows.recovery: Acceptance failure naming the field and listing what the form actually sends.
rows.evidence: Run 1's repo reports: 'the server requires a submitted field "items", but no form control is named "items"'.

rows.rootCause: Repairs were kept unconditionally. Measured decline 7.50 -> 7.16 -> 7.22 -> 6.94; the build could only walk away from its own best work and the LAST state was what the customer would receive.
rows.prevention: Repair ratchet: the best certified revision and its commit are tracked.
rows.detection: Each cycle's certified CX is compared with the best so far (epsilon 0.15 to ignore reviewer noise).

rows.evidence: Commit churn from the real build shows cycle 2's repair touched 11 files (+435/-219) for +0.06, and cycle 3's lost 0.28.
rows.note: No rollback mechanism exists in this repository.

rows.note: tar now runs with the workspace as its working directory and only relative paths, which both GNU tar and the bsdtar that Windows ships accept.
